body:
Fixes #8027.

`__Pyx_async_gen_athrow_throw()` and the error path of `__Pyx_async_gen_athrow_send_impl()` pass `PyErr_Occurred()` to `__Pyx_PyErr_GivenExceptionMatches2()` without a NULL check. When a throw into a pending `aclose()` makes the generator suspend again, no exception is set, so `exc_type` is NULL and the call reads `Py_TYPE(NULL)`.

This PR checks `exc_type` for NULL first at both sites, as `__Pyx_async_gen_unwrap_value()` already does. This matches CPython, which uses `PyErr_ExceptionMatches()` in `async_gen_athrow_throw`.

The new test `tests/run/asyncgen_aclose_throw.pyx` throws into a pending `aclose()` while the generator awaits in its `finally` block:

- master: `runtests.py asyncgen_aclose_throw` segfaults (exit 139)
- this branch: the test passes
- the same code passes as plain Python

comment_data.body:
Could we rename this file to `.py` rather than `.pyx`? That would mean the tests also run under plain Python which gives a bit of assurance that we're matching Python behaviour. I don't think this file uses any Cython-specific syntax so it should be compatible.

(Obviously if there's any Python bugs here then we may need to exclude specific Python versions. The `pure3.x` tag does that (e.g. `pure3.11` to run on 3.11 or above). But deal with that if it happens)
This is raising alarm-bells for me because it looks to be returning `NULL` without an exception set
Good catch, that guard was wrong. `check_error` is only reached after a `NULL` return, so an exception is always set there, and I've reverted that part.

commit.message: Fix NULL dereference when throwing into a pending async generator aclose()
Only inspect the exception in athrow_throw() when it returns NULL, run the test in plain Python

Exclude asyncgen_aclose_throw on GraalPy

GraalPy's native async generators do not suspend on an await in a
finally block during aclose(), so the plain Python run of the test
fails. CPython's test_asyncgen aclose_07/08/09/12 fail on GraalPy
for the same reason.
